# segmantR ![segmantR logo](reference/figures/logo-with-name.png)

segmantR segments microscopy images, records reproducible segmentation
protocols, and exchanges masks and measurements with downstream tools.
The core threshold and watershed workflows use R; optional external
engines require their own runtimes and model validation.

## Installation

segmantR is not on CRAN yet. Install it from GitHub:

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("CTTIR/segmantR")
```

See the declared R and package requirements in
[DESCRIPTION](https://github.com/CTTIR/segmantR/blob/main/DESCRIPTION).
Installing the R package does not install Python engines or download
models.

## Reproducible protocols and exchange

Besides the direct segmentation functions
([`sg_segment_threshold()`](https://cttir.github.io/segmantR/reference/sg_segment_threshold.md),
[`sg_segment_watershed()`](https://cttir.github.io/segmantR/reference/sg_segment_watershed.md),
[`sg_segment_propagate()`](https://cttir.github.io/segmantR/reference/sg_segment_propagate.md)
and the optional Cellpose, StarDist and Mesmer wrappers), segmantR
provides:

- **Versioned declarative protocols** (`segmantR-protocol-v1`):
  `threshold.otsu.v1`, `threshold.adaptive.v1`, `threshold.triangle.v1`,
  `watershed.distance.v1`, `watershed.h_minima.v1`,
  `propagate.voronoi.v1`, `postprocess.label-cleanup.v1` and the
  optional `stardist.2d.v1`, `cellpose.2d.v1`, `mesmer.2d.v1`.
  Parameters are whitelisted and every run records the exact delegate
  call.
- **A neutral interchange format** (`segmantR-interchange-v1`): JSON
  manifests, exact integer label TIFF, pixel-edge GeoJSON with stable
  object ids, measurement tables with explicit special values, and
  SHA-256 inventories. Imports are staged; reviewed masks are protected.
- **Training datasets and model bundles** with grouped, leakage-free
  splits, model cards, runtime descriptions and checksums.
- **QuPath programs**: readable Groovy templates driven by `run.json`
  for the Script Editor and `QuPath script`, and a StarDist parameter
  adapter.

``` r

library(segmantR)
img <- sg_example_image("fluorescence_nuclei")
run <- sg_protocol_run(img, "threshold.otsu.v1", min_area = 5L, output = "run")
bundle <- sg_export_interchange(run, tempfile("bundle"), image = img)
back <- sg_import_interchange(bundle$path, expected_digest = bundle$bundle_digest)
sg_mask_status(back$mask)$status  # "staged"
```

The core runs without Python, QuPath or EBImage; optional backends are
checked when used. Current capability status:

| Contract | Status |
|----|----|
| Neutral files and inventories (I0) | supported |
| Protocols and run envelopes (I1) | supported |
| Model bundles, training datasets | supported |
| QuPath programs, StarDist in QuPath | planned (headless runs verified with QuPath 0.7.0 and StarDist extension 0.6.0; no partner consumer yet) |
| Local control service | planned |

See
[`vignette("protocols-and-interop", package = "segmantR")`](https://cttir.github.io/segmantR/articles/protocols-and-interop.md)
and `system.file("interop", "INTEROP.md", package = "segmantR")`.

## Use of LLM tools

Where applicable, LLM tools were used for narrowly defined,
non-authorial tasks: copyediting, prose refinement, Markdown/LaTeX
formatting, boilerplate scaffolding (such as CI configurations and build
scripts), and code refactoring. Tools included [Chat
AI](https://kisski.gwdg.de/leistungen/2-02-llm-service/), the KISSKI
(GWDG) service, and self-hosted **Mistral Small (24B, Apache-2.0)**
served through a local **vLLM architecture** on an Ubuntu Linux
workstation with Intel processors and NVIDIA GPUs. The self-hosted model
ran locally, with no data sent to third parties.

All scientific claims, methodological choices, analyses, interpretations
and conclusions remain the authors’ own. Where applicable, LLM-generated
material must be reviewed and revised before inclusion, and references
must be verified against their DOI, arXiv ID or ISBN.

Local software setup: vLLM with Python/PyTorch, plus R and RStudio.

## Package responsibility

segmantR owns microscopy cell/nucleus segmentation, manual annotation
and correction, model training, review and QuPath exchange.
`hyperannotatR` (formerly annotatR) owns HSI annotation and evolves
independently.

The offline cell drawing engine was adapted from annotatR under its MIT
license (copyright 2026 Raban Heller). Its JavaScript and CSS are
maintained here as `sgcanvas`; no annotatR or hyperannotatR runtime
dependency is needed. `sg_canvas(image, mask)` displays cell boundaries
and
[`sg_canvas_correct()`](https://cttir.github.io/segmantR/reference/sg_canvas_correct.md)
converts local pixel polygons into staged mask corrections. The app
exposes rectangle, polygon, freehand, circle, edit and erase tools when
htmlwidgets and magick are installed. Existing image origin/plane
metadata is retained.

## Histology ROI annotations

The `sg_roi_*` APIs represent vector annotations independently of
integer instance masks and without an HSI annotation package dependency:

``` r

frame <- sg_roi_frame(c(100, 80), pixel_size = c(0.5, 0.8), pixel_unit = "um")
roi <- sg_roi_rect(10, 10, 30, 25, label = "tissue")
layer <- sg_roi_layer_add(sg_roi_layer("review"), roi)
project <- sg_roi_project(frame, layer)
mask <- sg_roi_mask(project, type = "labelled")
sg_roi_mask_stats(mask, pixel_size = frame$pixel_size)
# sg_roi_write_qupath(project, "review.geojson")
# imported <- sg_roi_read_qupath("review.geojson")
```

Frames declare image dimensions, calibration and optional pyramid
levels; they load no pixel data. Geometry, layer editing and masks
preserve image coordinates (top-left origin, x right, y down). Existing
`sg_mask`/`sg_export_qupath` APIs remain available for instance-mask
workflows. The ROI transfer does not include the HSI application or
control service. See
`system.file("roi-transfer", "README.md", package = "segmantR")` for
provenance and limitations.

## Branding

Editable R sources and regeneration instructions are in
[tools/branding](https://github.com/CTTIR/segmantR/tree/main/tools/branding).

  : Select one analysis channel from an image
